_comment: Registry of candidate dataset sources. 'labels_confirmed' means a human has checked the source's real class folders against configs/class_mapping.json; non-PlantVillage sources start unconfirmed and are skipped by preprocessing until confirmed (see README, 'Wheat and rice data'). Licence fields are what could be established; ALWAYS read the source's own terms before use or redistribution.

plantvillage.name: PlantVillage (colour images, 38 classes)
plantvillage.labels_confirmed_note: Verified 2026-10-29 by listing the 38 folders under raw/color at the pinned commit; they equal the 38 PlantVillage class keys in class_mapping.json exactly (54,305 files).
plantvillage.license: The GitHub repository contains no LICENSE file; it describes the data as an open-access research dataset and asks for citation (CITATION.cff). Check the terms on the landing page before redistributing.
plantvillage.citation: Mohanty SP, Hughes DP, Salathe M (2016). Using Deep Learning for Image-Based Plant Disease Detection. Frontiers in Plant Science 7:1419. doi:10.3389/fpls.2016.01419
manual_instructions: Alternative if git is unavailable: download the colour PlantVillage images (for example the Kaggle dataset 'abdallahalidev/plantvillage-dataset', which needs a free Kaggle login and acceptance of its terms).
Then run:  python -m src.data_download ingest --source plantvillage --archive C:\path\to\plantvillage-dataset.zip
Only the COLOUR images are used; 'grayscale' and 'segmented' folders are ignored automatically.
Avoid the Kaggle 'New Plant Diseases Dataset (Augmented)': it contains offline-augmented copies of the same photos, which leak between train and validation sets.

wheat_wfd.name: Wheat Fungi Diseases (WFD) dataset
wheat_wfd.license: UNVERIFIED - read the terms on the dataset's own page before use.
wheat_wfd.citation: See the citation requested on the dataset page.
manual_instructions: 1. Open https://wfd.sysbio.ru/index.html in a browser and read the licence / usage terms.
2. Follow the site's own download procedure (registration or acceptance of terms may be required; this tool never bypasses that).

3. Extract so that images sit inside folders named after their disease label, e.g. data\raw\wheat_wfd\<label>\*.jpg  (or run: python -m src.data_download ingest --source wheat_wfd --archive C:\path\to\file.zip).
4. Run: python -m src.data_download review-labels --source wheat_wfd   and compare the folder names with the documentation.
5. Only if the labels are justified (e.g. 'brown rust' = leaf rust, 'yellow rust' = stripe rust) run: python -m src.data_download confirm-labels --source wheat_wfd

wheat_14155.name: Wheat Plant Diseases Dataset (reported 14,155 images; Kaggle-derived)
wheat_14155.license: UNVERIFIED - the GTS.ai / Zenodo listings only say the data is 'sourced from Kaggle'. Find the ORIGINAL Kaggle dataset page, read its licence and note the uploader before use or redistribution.
wheat_14155.citation: UNVERIFIED - cite the original Kaggle dataset (uploader and title) once identified.
manual_instructions: 1. Identify the original Kaggle dataset behind the 14,155-image 'Wheat Plant Diseases Dataset' (the GTS.ai page only says 'sourced from Kaggle'); read its licence, class descriptions and whether it contains augmented or merged copies of other datasets.
2. Download it yourself (free Kaggle login / acceptance of terms is required; this tool never bypasses that).

3. Extract into data\raw\wheat_14155\ (or run: python -m src.data_download ingest --source wheat_14155 --archive C:\path\to\file.zip). Images must sit in <label>\*.jpg; the label is the folder that directly contains the image (nested train\valid\<label> is fine).
4. Do NOT mix these images into data\raw\wheat_wfd.

5. Run: python -m src.data_download review-labels --source wheat_14155  - every folder will show 'unknown' until the 'wheat_14155' aliases are added to configs/class_mapping.json (only for labels the dataset documentation supports).
6. Only after that, run: python -m src.data_download confirm-labels --source wheat_14155

wheat_long_2023.name: Wheat disease images, small dataset (Long et al. 2023, John Innes Centre; 999 photos)
wheat_long_2023.license: CC BY 4.0 (Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.7573133). Attribution required. Not the official WFD2020 dataset.
wheat_long_2023.citation: Long MC, Hartley M, Morris RJ, Brown JKM (2023). Wheat disease images (small dataset). Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.7573133. Described in Plant Pathology 2023, doi:10.1111/ppa.13684.
manual_instructions: 1. Download 'Long 2023 Plant Path 999 photos.zip' from https://zenodo.org/records/7573133 (md5 1f8a7c660c2da137b957fb4edee3dd7d).
2. Run: python -m src.data_download ingest --source wheat_long_2023 --archive C:\path\to\Long 2023 Plant Path 999 photos.zip
3. Run: python -m src.data_download review-labels --source wheat_long_2023   and compare with the record/paper (healthy, brown rust, yellow rust, mildew, septoria).
4. Only if correct run: python -m src.data_download confirm-labels --source wheat_long_2023
5. Septoria has no canonical class and is excluded (listed in known_unsupported_source_labels).

rice_mendeley.name: Rice Leaf Disease Image Dataset (Mendeley Data n8jpkpfz5p v1)
rice_mendeley.license: UNVERIFIED - the licence is shown on the Mendeley Data page; read it before use.
rice_mendeley.citation: See the 'Cite this dataset' section on the Mendeley Data page.
manual_instructions: 1. Open https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/n8jpkpfz5p/1 in a browser, read the licence and click Download.

2. Extract so that images sit inside folders named after their disease label, e.g. data\raw\rice_mendeley\<label>\*.jpg  (or run: python -m src.data_download ingest --source rice_mendeley --archive C:\path\to\file.zip).
3. Run: python -m src.data_download review-labels --source rice_mendeley   and compare folder names with the dataset description.
4. Only when satisfied, run: python -m src.data_download confirm-labels --source rice_mendeley
